translations.text: After the death of Moses, the servant of the Lord, the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, Moses’ assistant, saying:
My servant Moses is dead. Now get up and cross this Jordan, you and all these people, into the land that I am giving you, the people of Israel.
Every place where your feet have walked I will give you, just as I told Moses.
Your territory shall extend from the wilderness and Anti-Lebanon to the great river, the Euphrates—all the land of the Hittites—and to the western sea, toward the setting sun.
No one will stand against you throughout your life. Just as I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not leave you or neglect you.
Be strong and courageous, for you will divide among these people the land that I swore to their ancestors I would give them.

Only be strong and very courageous, so that you keep and carry out the whole law, just as my servant Moses commanded you. Do not turn away from it to the right or to the left, so that you may act wisely wherever you go.

Do not let this book of the law depart from your mouth. Read it day and night, so that you may know how to do everything written in it. For you will make your path straight, and through it you will become wise.
Look, I command you: be courageous and strong. Do not be afraid or terrified, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
Joshua commanded the scribes of the people, saying:

Go through the camp and command the people, telling them: Prepare provisions for yourselves, for within three days you will cross this Jordan and enter to take the land that the Lord, the God of your ancestors, is giving you to possess.
Joshua also said to Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh:
Remember the command that Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave you when he told you: The Lord has given you rest and has given you this land.

Let your wives, your children, and your livestock remain in this land that Moses gave you beyond the Jordan. But you, all your strong men, must cross over armed ahead of your brothers and fight for them alongside them,

until the Lord our God gives your brothers rest as he has given you, and they too possess their land, which the Lord our God is giving them. Then each of you may return to his own inheritance, and you too may possess this land that Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave you beyond the Jordan, toward the rising sun.
They answered Joshua, saying: We will do everything you have commanded us, and we will go wherever you send us.
Just as we obeyed Moses in everything, so we will obey you too. Only may the Lord be with you as he was with Moses.
Anyone who disobeys you, rebels against you, and does not heed your commands shall die. Now be strong and courageous.

Joshua secretly sent two young men as spies from Shittim and told them, “Go up and inspect the land and Jericho.” The two young men went and entered Jericho. They entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab and stayed there.
They informed the king of Jericho, saying: Men from the people of Israel have come here tonight—spies who have come to inspect the land.
The king of Jericho sent messengers to Rahab, saying: Tell Rahab: Bring out the men who came to you at night and entered your house. They are spies, and they have come to inspect the land.
The woman took the two men and hid them. She said, “The men did come to me, but I did not know where they were from.”
When the gate was closed in the darkness, those men went out. I do not know where those men went. Go quickly, follow them, and pursue them; perhaps you will catch them.
But she had taken them up onto the roof and hidden them among the stalks of flax spread out there.
Those men pursued them without spending the night, while she went up to them on the roof.
She said to them, “I know that the Lord has handed the land over to you, for the Lord has brought fear of you upon us, and all who live in the land have melted away before you.

For we have heard how the Lord dried up the Red Sea before you when you came out of the land of Egypt, and everything he did to the kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you utterly destroyed.
When we heard, our hearts were terrified, and not one of us had any spirit left before you, for the Lord your God is God in heaven above and on earth below.
Now swear to me by the Lord that, just as I have shown you kindness, you will show kindness to me and to my father’s household, and give me a trustworthy sign.
Keep my father’s household alive, along with my mother, my brothers, my whole household, and all that belongs to them, and save our lives from death.”

The men said to her, “Our lives in place of yours, even to death!” She said to them, “When the Lord hands our city over to you, show me kindness and faithfulness.” The men said to her, “If you do not tell anyone about us, we will show you kindness and faithfulness when the Lord hands your city over to us.”
She lowered them by a rope through a window, for her house was in the wall, and she lived within its fortifications.
She said to them, “Go into the mountains so that those pursuing you will not find you. Hide there for three days, until your pursuers return, and afterward you can go on your way.”
The men said to her, “We are free of the oath you made us swear.
Look, when we enter the outskirts of the city, put this scarlet-red thread in the window through which you lowered us, and gather your father, your mother, and your brothers to you in your house.
Anyone who goes outside the door of your house will die, and we will be free of this oath you made us swear. But if anyone who is with you inside your house dies, the guilt will be upon us.
But if anyone betrays us and reveals our business, we will be free of this oath to you.”
She said to them, “Let it be as you have said.” She sent them away, and they left. Then she tied that scarlet sign in her window.
They went out into the mountains and stayed there for three days, until their pursuers returned. Their pursuers searched for them along every road but did not find them.
The men returned, came down from the mountain, crossed over, and reached Joshua son of Nun. They told him everything they had done.
They said to Joshua, “The Lord has handed the whole land over to us, and all the peoples who live in that land are terrified of us.”
Joshua rose early in the morning, and they set out from Shittim. He and all the Israelites reached the Jordan and camped there before crossing over.
After three days, the scribes went through the camp.
They gave instructions to the people, saying, “When you see the ark of the law of the Lord our God, with our priests and our Levites carrying it, you too must set out from your places and follow it.

But keep a distance of about two thousand cubits between yourselves and it. Stay at that measured distance and do not approach it, so that you may know the way you are to go, for you have not traveled this way before.”
Joshua said to the people, “Purify yourselves for tomorrow, for tomorrow the Lord will do wonders for you.”
Joshua said to the priests, “Take up the ark of the law of the Lord and go ahead of the people.” So the priests took up the ark of the law of the Lord and went ahead of the people.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Look, today I will begin to make you great before all the Israelites, so that they may know that I am with you as I was with Moses.
Now command the priests who carry the ark and tell them, ‘When you enter the edge of the waters of the Jordan, stand there in the Jordan.’”
Joshua said to the Israelites, “Come here and hear the word of the Lord our God.”

Joshua said to them, “By this you will know that the living God is with you and that he will completely destroy before you the Canaanites, [the Hittites,] the Perizzites, the Hivites, the Amorites, the Jebusites, and the Girgashites.
Look, the ark of the law of the Lord of all the earth [is crossing ahead of you] over the Jordan.
Choose twelve men for yourselves from among the Israelites, one man from each tribe.

When the priests who carry the ark of the law of the Lord of all the earth set their feet in the waters of the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan will dry up, and the water coming down from above will stand still.”
Then, when the people set out from their camp to cross the Jordan, the priests carried the ark of the law and went ahead of the people.

When the priests carrying the ark of the law entered the Jordan, and the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the law dipped into the edge of the Jordan’s waters—the Jordan was full up to its banks, as in the rainy season and when the wheat ripens—

the water coming down from above stood still. It stood like a [?], extending very, very far away, as far as the territory of Kiriath-jearim. The water flowing downstream went down into the Sea of the Arabah, the Sea of Alon, and dried up, leaving dry ground. The people stood opposite Jericho.

The priests carrying the ark of the Lord’s law stood firmly on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan. All the Israelites crossed over on dry ground until the entire people had finished crossing the Jordan.
When all the people had finished crossing the Jordan, the Lord said to Joshua,
“Take twelve men, one man from each tribe.”
He commanded them to take twelve round stones from there, from the middle of the Jordan where the priests’ feet stood: “Carry them with you and keep them in your camps, where you stay tonight.”
Joshua summoned twelve men from among the distinguished men of the Israelites, one man from each tribe.

Joshua said to them, “Come and bring before me and before the Lord from the middle of the Jordan. Each of you is to take one stone from there and carry it on your shoulder, according to the number of the twelve tribes of Israel,
so that they may be a sign for you and remain with you always. When your son asks you in the future, ‘What do these stones mean to you?’
tell your son, ‘The Jordan River dried up before the ark of the law of the Lord of all the earth as it crossed.’ These stones will be a memorial for you Israelites forever.”

The Israelites did as the Lord had commanded Joshua. They took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, as the Lord had commanded Joshua, when the Israelites had finished crossing. They kept them with them in their camp and placed them there.
Joshua set up another twelve stones in the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the law had stood. They remain there until today, to this very day.

The priests carrying the ark of the law stood in the middle of the Jordan until Joshua had completed everything the Lord had commanded Joshua to tell the people, according to everything Moses had commanded Joshua. The people hurried across.
When the people had finished crossing, the ark of the law also crossed, along with those stones that were before them.
The descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh crossed, armed, ahead of the Israelites, as Moses had commanded them.
[400–100] [?], equipped for battle, crossed before the Lord to fight against the city of Jericho.
On that day the Lord made Joshua great before all the people of Israel, and they feared him as they had feared Moses, throughout his lifetime.
The Lord said to Joshua:
“Command the priests carrying the ark of the Lord’s law to come up out of the Jordan.”
[Joshua commanded the priests and said to them, “Come up out of the Jordan.”]

When the priests carrying the ark of the Lord’s law came up from the middle of the Jordan and set their feet on the ground, the water of the Jordan rushed back to its place and flowed as before, reaching its banks.
On the tenth day of the first month, the people came up out of the Jordan, and the Israelites camped at Gilgal, east of Jericho.
Joshua set up those twelve stones at Gilgal.
Joshua said to the Israelites, “When your children ask you, ‘What are these stones?’
tell your children, ‘We crossed this Jordan on dry ground.'
For the Lord dried up the water of the Jordan before us until we crossed, just as the Lord did to the Red Sea, which the Lord our God dried up before us until we had passed through,
so that all the nations of the earth might know that the Lord’s power is mighty, and so that you too might fear the Lord our God in everything you do.”

Then, when all the kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan toward the sea, and all the kings of the Phoenicians along the sea, heard that the Lord had dried up the Jordan River before the Israelites so that they could cross, their hearts melted and collapsed, and they were at a loss about what to think in the face of the Israelites.
After those days, the Lord said to Joshua, “Make yourself stone knives from flint, sit down, and circumcise the Israelites again.”
Joshua made himself flint knives and circumcised the Israelites at the place called the Hill of Foreskins.

This was why Joshua circumcised them: all the people who had come out of Egypt—all their males, the fighting men who died in the wilderness on the journey after leaving Egypt—[had been circumcised]. But all the people born along the way in the wilderness after leaving the land of Egypt had not been circumcised.
So that Joshua might purify the Israelites, all those born along the way and all those who had not been circumcised when they came out of Egypt.

Joshua circumcised all these, because Israel had wandered for forty years in the wilderness of Madbara. Most of the fighting men who came out of the land of Egypt had not been circumcised. They had rejected the Lord’s command, and the Lord said to them, “You will not see that land which the Lord swore to our fathers that he would give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.”
In their place he raised up their children, whom Joshua circumcised, because they were uncircumcised: they had been born along the way and had not been circumcised.
When they had been circumcised, they remained in the camp until they recovered.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Look, today, on this day, I have removed the reproach of Egypt from you.” He named that place Gilgal, as it is called to this very day.
The Israelites camped in Gilgal, and the Israelites celebrated the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, on the plains of Jericho, across the Jordan, in the wilderness.
They ate from the produce of the land, unleavened bread and fresh grain.
On that day the manna stopped. On the next day they ate the produce of the land, and the Israelites no longer found manna, for they harvested the land of Phoenicia that year.
While Joshua was in Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing before him with a drawn sword in his hand. Joshua approached him and said, “Are you one of our people or one of our enemies?”

He said to him, “I am the angel of the Lord’s army, and now I have arrived.” Joshua fell on his face to the ground and bowed before him. He said to him, “Why have you taken your stand before your servant?”
The angel of the Lord’s army said to Joshua, “Take your sandals off your feet, because the place where you are standing is holy ground.” Joshua did so.
Jericho was closed and fortified, and no one went out of it and no one went in.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Look, I will deliver Jericho into your hands, along with its king and those within it who are strong and mighty.
You are to position all the fighting men around it. All the fighting men are to march around the city, making one circuit of that city at a time. Do this for six days.
Seven priests shall carry seven jubilee horns before the ark. On the seventh day they shall circle the city seven times, and the priests shall blow those horns.

When they blow those jubilee horns, as soon as you hear the sound of the horn, let all the people shout together. As soon as they shout, the city’s wall itself will fall down beneath them. Then let all the people enter, each one running straight ahead into the city.”
Joshua went to the priests and said to them, “Take up the ark of the law, and let seven priests carry seven jubilee trumpets before the Lord.”
He said to them, “Command the people to go and march around the city, and let the fighting men also go with their weapons before the ark of the Lord.”
As Joshua had told the people, the seven priests took seven sacred trumpets to go before the Lord. As they went, they blew loudly as a signal, and the ark of the Lord’s law followed them.
The fighting men marched on to the end, and the priests blew the trumpets. Those bringing up the rear marched behind the ark of the Lord’s law, blowing a horn.
Joshua commanded the people not to make any noise, not to let anyone hear their voices, and not to let a word come out of their mouths until he commanded them to shout.
The ark of the Lord’s law went around the city. Then it returned to the camp and spent the night there.
On the second day Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests carried the ark of the Lord’s law.

Seven priests took seven trumpets and went before the ark of the Lord. Then the fighting men followed, and then the rest of the people followed. They marched behind the ark of the Lord’s law, blowing horns, while the priests blew the trumpets.
All the rest of the people marched around the city on the second day, approaching it. Then they returned to the camp again. They did this for six days.
On the seventh day they rose at daybreak and marched around the city in the same way seven times. Only on that day did they march around the city seven times.
When they had marched around the city seven times, the priests blew their trumpets, and Joshua said to the Israelites, “Shout, because the Lord has delivered it to us!

We have devoted this city to destruction, and everything in it shall belong to the Lord of hosts, except Rahab the prostitute. You shall keep her alive, along with everyone in her house, because she hid the spies whom we sent.

But you must take care not to take anything from what is devoted to destruction, which we have devoted to destruction. Do not covet it or take anything from it. Otherwise you will make the camp of the Israelites accursed and bring trouble upon us.
All the gold, all the silver, the bronze, and the iron must be holy to the LORD and must go into the LORD’s treasury.

The people shouted, and the priests sounded the trumpets. All the people together gave a great and mighty shout, and all the walls surrounding the city fell down. All the people entered the city, each rushing straight ahead, and they captured the city.
Joshua devoted the city and everything in it to destruction. They killed everyone with the sword, men and women, young and old, as well as cattle, sheep, and donkeys.
Joshua said to the two young spies who had explored the land, “Go into that prostitute’s house and bring her out of there, along with everyone who is with her, just as you swore to her.”

The two young spies who had explored the city went into the woman’s house. They brought out Rahab the prostitute, her father, her mother, her brothers, all her relatives, and everything that belonged to her. They brought her outside the camp of Israel.
The city and everything in it were burned with fire, except for the gold, silver, and all the bronze and iron, which they gathered and brought into the treasury of the LORD’s house.

Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute and her father’s entire household. She has lived among Israel until today, to this very day, because she hid the spies whom Joshua sent to explore the city of Jericho.

On that day Joshua imposed an oath, saying, “Cursed be anyone who rebuilds this city! At the cost of his firstborn son he will lay its foundations, and at the cost of his youngest son he will set up its gates.” Ozen of Bethel did just that: at the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundations, and at the cost of his youngest surviving son he set up its gates.
The Lord was with Joshua, and his name became known throughout the whole land.

The Israelites committed a great sin and took some of what they had devoted to destruction. Achan son of Carmi, son of Zimri, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of what they had devoted to destruction, and the LORD became angry with the Israelites.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is near Bethel, east of Bethel. He told them, “Go up and explore Ai.” So the men went up and explored Ai.

They returned to Joshua and told him, “Do not let all the people go up. Let two or three thousand men go up and fight against that city. Do not send all the people there, for its inhabitants are few.”
About three thousand of the people went up, but the men of Ai drove them back, and they fled before them.
They killed thirty-six of their men in Ai. Then they pursued them from the gate until they had destroyed them, killing them on the descent. The people’s hearts were terrified and became like water.
Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown on the ground before the ark of the Lord until evening, together with the elders of Israel. They put dust on their heads.

Joshua said, “I beg you, Lord, Lord, why did your servant ever bring this people across the Jordan, only for you to hand them over to the Amorites and destroy us? If only we had camped and remained on the other side of the Jordan!
Lord, what can I say now? Look, Israel has turned its back on its enemy!
When the Canaanites and all who live in this land hear of it, they will surround us and wipe us off the earth. What will you do for your great name?”
The Lord said to Joshua, “Get up! Why are you lying facedown?”
The people have sinned and broken the covenant I made with them. They have taken some of what was devoted to destruction, stolen it, and put it among their own possessions.

So the Israelites cannot stand before their enemies, but turn their backs before their enemies, because they have become accursed. He will no longer be with you unless you remove the accursed thing from among you.

Rise, consecrate the people, and let them purify themselves for tomorrow, for this is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Something devoted to destruction is among you. You cannot stand before your enemies until you remove from among you what is devoted to destruction.

They shall rise in the morning and all assemble by their tribes. The tribe that the Lord points out shall separate and stand by its clans. The clan that the Lord points out shall separate and stand by its households. The household that the Lord points out shall separate and stand man by man.
The man whom he points out shall be burned with fire, along with everything belonging to him, because he has betrayed the covenant of the Lord and committed a sin against Israel.
Joshua rose early and assembled the people by their tribes, and the tribe of Judah was singled out.
Those from Judah separated by their clans, and the clan of Zerah was singled out. The clan of Zerah separated by its households, and the household of Zimri was singled out.
The household of Zimri separated man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zerah, from Judah, was singled out.
Joshua said to Achan, “My son, give praise to the Lord, the God of Israel, and confess to him. Tell me what you have done, and do not hide it from me.”
Achan answered Joshua and said to him, “Truly, I have sinned before the Lord, the God of Israel. This is what I did:

When I saw among the plunder a shaggy garment, two hundred didrachms of silver (coins), and a tongue-shaped bar of gold equivalent in weight to fifty didrachms, I coveted them and took them. Look, they are buried in my tent, and the silver coins are buried underneath.”
Joshua sent his young men, and they ran to the place [?] in his tent. These things were buried in his tent, and the silver was there with them, underneath.
They brought them out of his tent and took them to Joshua and all the elders of Israel, and laid them before the Lord.

Joshua took Achan son of Zerah, the silver, the garment, and the tongue-shaped bar of gold, and brought them into the Valley of Achor. He also took his sons, his daughters, his cattle, his sheep, his donkeys, his tent, and all his possessions, and brought them into the Valley of Achor.
Joshua said to Achan, “Why have you brought trouble on us? May the Lord bring trouble on you this very day!” All Israel stoned him with stones. They burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.

They set up a stone monument for him, which remains to this day, to this very day. The Lord turned away from his fierce anger. For this reason he called it the Valley of Achor, as it is called to this day, to this very day.

The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid or dismayed. Take all the fighting men with you, rise, and go up to Ai. Look, I have delivered into your hands the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.
Do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king. Take their livestock as plunder for yourself. But send men to lie in ambush behind the city.”
Joshua and all the fighting men rose and went up to Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand strong, mighty fighting men and sent them out by night.
He commanded them, saying, “Go, and see to it that you lie in ambush behind the city. Do not go very far from the city, and all of you remain ready.”
I and everyone with me will advance toward the city. When the men of Ai come out to meet us, we will flee before them as we did before.
When they come out and pursue us, we will draw them away from the city. They will say, ‘These men too are fleeing before us as before.’ And we will flee before them.
Then you too must rise up and destroy their city, and the Lord your God will deliver it into your hands.
When you have entered their city, burn it with fire. Do as I have told you. Look, I have given you your orders.
Joshua sent them out, and they went to lie in ambush. They took up their position between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai. Joshua spent that night there among the people.
Joshua rose early in the morning and inspected the people. He and the elders of Israel went up at the very front of the people against Ai.

All the fighting men went up with him. They went and arrived in front of the city, on its eastern side. Those who lay in ambush for the city were on the side toward the east of the sea [?]. They took up their position north of Ai, with a valley between them and Ai.
He took five thousand men and stationed them in ambush between Bethon and Ai, west of Ai.
All the people camped, with their encampments north of the city and their flank extending to the west of the city. That night Joshua went into the middle of that valley.

When the king of Ai heard this, he rose quickly. The men of the city came out to meet those in front of them and fight them—he and all the people with him—at that time, facing the Arabah. But he did not know that an ambush had been set for them behind the city.
When they reached them, Joshua and all Israel fled before them and escaped along the road into the wilderness.
All the people of the land rallied and followed them, chasing and pursuing the Israelites.
They were far from the city, and no one remained in Ai or Bethel who had not followed and pursued Israel. They left the city open and chased and pursued Israel.

The Lord said to Joshua, ‘Raise your hand with the spear that is in your hand toward Ai, for I have delivered it into your hand. Let those lying in ambush rise quickly from their positions.’ Joshua raised his hand with the spear toward the city.
Those lying in ambush rose quickly from their positions and came out when he raised his hand with the spear. They entered the city, captured it, and quickly set it on fire.

When the men of Ai looked behind them and saw smoke rising into the sky from their city, they found nowhere to flee, either this way or that. The people who had fled into the wilderness turned against those pursuing them.
Joshua saw that those who had lain in ambush had captured the city. They knew it when they saw smoke rising from the city into the sky. Then they turned back and killed the people of Ai.

The others also came out of the city to meet them and brought them into the midst of Israel’s encampments. They killed them, some from this side and others from that side, until they left no survivor who escaped.
They captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

When the Israelites had finished killing the men of Ai in the wilderness and on the mountain slope where they had pursued them, killing them all with the sword and destroying them, Joshua then returned to Ai and struck it with the sword.
All those who died at that time, men and women, numbered twelve thousand—all the people of Ai.
Joshua did not lower the hand he had raised with the spear until they had destroyed the people of Ai.
Except for the livestock and all the plunder of the city, which the Israelites took for themselves by the Lord’s command, just as the Lord had commanded Joshua.
Joshua burned the city with fire, and it became dust. He made it permanently uninhabited, down to today, to this very day.

He hung the king of Ai on a cedar tree, and he remained on the tree until evening. When the sun set, Joshua gave orders, and they took him down from the tree and stoned him in a pit at the city gate. They made for him a great [?] of stones, which remains to this very day.

When all the kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan heard of it—those in the mountains, those in the wilderness, those along the entire shore of the Great Sea, and those in the Anti-Lebanon—the Hittites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Amorites, Girgashites, and Jebusites;
They gathered together to fight against Joshua and all Israel.
At that time Joshua built an altar to the Lord, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,

as Moses, the servant of the Lord, had commanded the Israelites, as it is written in the law of Moses: an altar of whole stones, neither carved nor worked with iron. On it he offered an offering to the Lord and sacrifices of well-being.
Joshua wrote on the stones this Deuteronomy, the law of Moses, which he wrote before all the Israelites.

All Israel, with their leaders and scribes, walked on the left and right before the ark, while the priests and Levites carried the ark of the Lord’s law. Half of them, including both resident foreigners and native-born people, were near Mount Ebal, and half were near Mount Gerizim, as Moses, the servant of the Lord, had commanded them to bless the people of Israel.
They stood there, and after this Joshua read all the words of this law, its blessings and its curses, everything written in the law of Moses.

There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded Joshua that Joshua did not read and make heard by the whole assembly of the Israelites—their men, their women, their children, and the resident foreigners who traveled with Israel (and all Israel).
The inhabitants of Gibeon heard everything that the Lord had done to Jericho and Ai.
They too acted cunningly. They came supplied with provisions and prepared themselves, carrying old provision bags on their shoulders and old wineskins, torn and patched.

The straps of their sandals were broken, and the sandals on their feet were old and patched. The clothes they wore were also old, and the bread they had brought for provisions was dry, moldy, and worm-eaten.
They came to Joshua in the assembly of Israel at Gilgal and said to Joshua and all Israel, “We have come from a distant land. Now make a sworn agreement with us.”
The Israelites said to the Horites, “How can we make a sworn agreement with you? [?] You live nearby.”
They said to Joshua, “We are your servants.” He said to them, “Where are you from, and where have you come from?”
They said to him, “We, your servants, have come from a very distant land because of the name of the Lord your God, for we have heard about him and everything he did to the Egyptians,
and everything he did to the two kings of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan: Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
When we heard, our elders and all the people of our land told us, ‘Take provisions for the journey and go to meet them. Tell them, “We are your servants. Now make a sworn agreement with us.”’
Look at this bread of ours: it was still warm when we took it from our homes on the day we set out to come to you. But now it is worm-eaten and dry.
These wineskins of ours were new when we filled them, but now they are empty, worn out, and torn. Our clothes and sandals have also worn out, because the journey was very long.”
The leaders took some of their provisions, but they did not inquire of the Lord.
Joshua made peace with them and entered into a sworn agreement with them to spare their lives. The representatives of the assembly also swore an oath to them.
Three days after they had sworn an oath to them, they heard that these people were nearby and lived among them.
The Israelites set out and reached their cities on the third day. Their cities were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.

The Israelites did not fight them, because all the leaders of the assembly had sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. The whole assembly of the Israelites grumbled against their leaders.
All the leaders said to the whole assembly, “We have sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, and now we cannot touch them in any way.
But this is what we will do: we will let them live and make them our servants, so that wrath will not come upon us because of the oath we swore to them.”
The leaders said to them, “We have spared your lives and appointed you to chop wood and draw water for the whole assembly.” This is what the leaders commanded them.
Joshua summoned them and said to them, “Why did you deceive me and tell me, ‘We are very far away from you,’ when you are neighbors of those who live among us?”
Now you are cursed. There shall never cease to be slaves among you who cut wood and draw water for me and for my God.

They answered him, “We were clearly told everything that the LORD your God said to Moses his servant: that he would give you this land and destroy us and everyone living in it before you. That is why we did this.
Now, here we are in your hands. Do to us whatever you wish and whatever seems good to you.”
Joshua saved them that day.

He likewise made them wood carriers and water carriers for the whole assembly and for the altar of the LORD. For this reason, the people of Gibeon have been wood carriers and water carriers for the whole assembly and for the altar of the LORD until today, even to this day, and for the place that the LORD chose.

When Adoni-bezek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and destroyed it, doing to Ai and its king just as he had done to Jericho and its king, and that the people of Gibeon had defected and come over to Joshua and Israel and were living among them,
they were very afraid of them, because they knew that Gibeon was a very large city, like one of the royal cities. It was larger than Ai, and all its men were strong.
Adoni-bezek king of Jerusalem sent to Elam king of Hebron, Phidon king of Jarmuth, Jephthah king of Lachish, and Debit king of Adullam, saying,
“Come up to me and help me, so that we may attack Gibeon, whose people have gone over to Joshua and the Israelites.”

These five kings of the Jebusites gathered and went up: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Adullam. They and all their forces besieged Gibeon and attacked it.

The people of Gibeon sent word to Joshua in the camp of Israel at Gilgal, saying, “Do not withhold your help from your servants. Come up to us quickly, help us, and save us, because all the kings of the Amorites who live in the mountains have gathered against us.”
Joshua went up from Gilgal with all the fighting men and all his mighty warriors.
The LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, for I will deliver them into your hands. Not one of them will survive before you.”
Joshua came upon them suddenly at night, having departed from Gilgal.

The LORD threw them into panic before Israel, and the LORD struck them down in a great slaughter at Gibeon. The Israelites pursued them along the road up to Beth-horon and struck them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

And as they fled before the Israelites down the descent of Beth-horon, the Lord pelted them with hailstones from heaven as far as Azekah. More died from the hailstones than the Israelites killed with their swords in battle.

At that time Joshua spoke to the Lord, when the Lord delivered the Amorites into the hands of the Israelites, when they crushed them at Gibeon and they were crushed before Israel. Joshua said, “Let the sun stand still over Gibeon, and the moon over the valley of Aijalon.”

The sun and the moon stood still in their positions where they were, until the Lord destroyed their enemies. This was written in this book at that time. The sun stood still in the middle of the sky and did not move toward the west for a whole day.
There was no day like that day, either before it or after it, when the Lord answered the voice of a human being, for the Lord fought for Israel.
Joshua and all Israel with him returned to the camp at Gilgal.
Those five kings fled and hid in a cave at Makkedah.
They reported to Joshua, saying, “Those five kings have been found in the cave at Makkedah where they hid.”
Joshua said to them, “Roll a large stone against the mouth of that cave, and station men over them to guard them.
But you must not stop. Pursue all your enemies to the very last of them, and do not let them enter their cities, for the Lord our God has delivered them into our hands.”
After this, when Joshua and all Israel had finished killing them in a very great slaughter beyond counting, those of them who escaped fled and entered fortified towns.
All the people returned safely to Joshua at the camp in Makkedah. No one uttered a word against the Israelites.
Joshua said to them, “Open that cave and bring those five kings out of the cave to me.”
They did so and brought those five kings out of the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Adullam.

They brought them to Joshua. Joshua summoned all Israel, those who had fought and those who had gone with him, and said to them, “Go and put your feet on their necks.” And they put their feet on their necks.
Joshua said to them, “Do not fear them or be terrified of them. Be courageous and strong, for this is what the Lord will do to all your enemies against whom you fight.”
After this Joshua killed them, and they pierced them and hung them on five trees. They remained hanging on the trees until evening.

Then, when the sun had set, Joshua gave the order, and they took them down from those trees and threw them into the cave into which they had fled. They rolled large stones over the cave, and they remain there to this very day.

They also captured Makkedah that day and killed its people and its king with the sword. They destroyed every living person in it and left no one breathing there, not even one; no one escaped. They did to the king of Makkedah as they had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua and all Israel with him went from Makkedah to Libnah.

The Lord delivered it into the hands of Israel. They captured it and captured its king, and Joshua killed him with the sword. He left nothing alive in it; not a single fugitive escaped from among them. They did to its king as they had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua and all Israel with him went from Libnah to Lachish. They camped against it and fought against it.
The Lord delivered Lachish into the hands of Israel. They captured it on the second day, killed its people with the sword, and destroyed it as they had done to Libnah.
At that time Elam, king of Gezer, came up to help Lachish. Joshua killed him and his people with the sword, until he left no fugitive among them and no one escaped.
Joshua and all Israel with him went from Lachish to Adullam. They camped against it and fought against it.
The Lord delivered it into the hands of Israel. They captured it that day and struck it with the sword. They killed every living being in it, just as they had done to Lachish.
Joshua and all Israel with him went to Hebron and camped against it.
They struck it with the sword, together with every living person in it, and no one escaped. As they had done to Adullam, they destroyed it together with everyone in it.
Joshua and all Israel returned to Debir and encamped against it.

They captured it, its king, and its towns. They struck it down and destroyed it with the edge of the sword, along with every breathing creature in it. They left no survivor in it. Just as they had done to Hebron and its king, so they did to Debir and its king.

Joshua struck down their entire land: the hill country, the Negeb, its plains, the slopes, and its kings. They left no survivor among them. He destroyed everything that had the breath of life, as the Lord, the God of Israel, had commanded,
from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and all Goshen as far as Gibeon.
Joshua defeated all their kings and their lands at once, because the Lord fought for Israel.
[Joshua and all Israel with him returned to the camp at Gilgal.]
When Jabin, king of Hazor, heard this, he sent word to Jobab, king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph,
and to the kings toward Great Sidon, (those) in the mountains, in the Arabah opposite Chinnereth, in the plains, and in Naphoth-dor,
and to the coastal Canaanites in the east, and to the coastal Amorites, Hivites, Jebusites, and Perizzites in the mountains, and to the Hittites in the plains and in Meseumen [?].
They came out, with their kings accompanying them, as numerous as the sand of the sea, [with very many horses and chariots].
All their kings gathered and came together, joining forces to fight Israel by the waters of Merom.

The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, because tomorrow at this [time] I will hand them over to be killed before Israel. Cut the hamstrings of their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”
Joshua and all the fighting men went against them at the waters of Merom and fell upon them, coming down on them from the mountains.

The Lord handed them over to Israel. They pursued them, killing them as far as Great Sidon, as far as Maseron [?], and as far as the plains of Mizpah to the east. They killed them, leaving none of them to escape.
Joshua did to them as the Lord had commanded him: he cut the hamstrings of their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
At that time Joshua turned back and captured Hazor and its king, because Hazor had formerly ruled over all these kings.
They killed every breathing creature in it with the sword and destroyed them all, leaving nothing that breathed in it. He burned Hazor with fire, along with all the cities of the kings.
Joshua captured their kings, killed them with the sword, and utterly destroyed them, as Moses, the Lord’s servant, had commanded him.
But Israel did not burn the other cities throughout all the regions. Hazor alone was the one Israel burned.
The Israelites took all its plunder for themselves. But they slaughtered all the people, destroying them with the sword, and left not a single living person among them.
As the Lord had commanded his servant Moses, Moses commanded Joshua, and Joshua did likewise. He left nothing undone of all that Moses had commanded him.

Joshua took the whole territory of their land toward the mountains, all the land of Adeb [?], all the land of Goshen and its plains, the territory toward its west, the mountain of Israel, and their territory below toward the mountain.
From Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, as far as Baal-gad and the fields of Lebanon toward Mount Hermon, he captured all their kings, killed them, and destroyed them.
Joshua remained a long time fighting against these kings.
There was no city that Israel did not capture. They captured them all in battle.
For the Lord hardened their hearts to fight against Israel, so that Israel would utterly destroy them and show them no mercy, but wipe them out, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

In those days Joshua went and destroyed the Anakim in the mountains, from Hebron, Debir, and Anab, and from all the territory of Israel and the mountains of Judah, together with their cities. Joshua destroyed them.
He left none of the Anakim in Israel, except those who remained in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
Joshua took all their land, as the Lord had commanded Moses. Joshua gave it to Israel as their inheritance, dividing it among their tribes. Then the land rested from war.

These are the kings whom the Israelites killed and whose land they took possession of beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise, from the valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon, including all the land of the Arabah to the east:
Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon and ruled from Arnon, which lies in the valley [?], and over half of Gilead as far as the Jabbok, the border of the Ammonites;

And the Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinnereth on the east, and as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, on its eastern side, along the road toward Jeshimoth, and southward below Medoth and Pisgah.
and Og king of Bashan, who remained from among the giants who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.

He ruled from the mountains of Hermon and from Salecah, over all Bashan as far as the territories of the Girgashites and the Maacathites, and over half of Gilead as far as the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses the servant of the Lord and the Israelites killed them. Moses gave that land as an inheritance to Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

These are the kings of the Amorites whom Joshua and the Israelites killed beyond the Jordan to the west, from Baal-gad in the wilderness of Lebanon to Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir. Joshua gave that land to the people of Israel as an inheritance and put them in possession of it:
in the mountains, in the wilderness, in the Arabah, on the slopes, in the fields, and in the Negev; and the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Hivites.
The king of Jericho and the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel;
The king of Jerusalem; the king of Hebron.
the king of Jarmuth; the king of Lachish;
the king of Elam; the king of Gezer;
the king of Debir; the king of Gisir;
the king of Hormah; the king of Arad;
the king of Libnah; the king of Adullam;
the king of Edah;
the king of Etaphad; the king of Hepher;
the king of Aphek-tesaroth; the king of Asom;
the king of Shimron; the king of Memroth;
the king of Achshaph; the king of Kedesh;
the king of Zeqeq; the king of Meredoth;
the king of Jokneam in Carmel; the king of Dor in Naphath-dor;
the king of Gai in Galilee; the king of Tirzah.
All these kings numbered twenty-nine.
Joshua grew old, and his days had passed. The Lord said to Joshua, “Look, your days have passed, and much land remains to be possessed.
This is the land that remains: the territories of the Philistines, the Geshurites, and the Canaanites,

from the wilderness facing Egypt to the territory of Ekron, on the left of the Amorites, reckoned as belonging to the five districts of the Philistines: Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, the Gittites, Ekron, and the Avvites;
from the south, and all the land of Canaan opposite Gaza, and Sidon as far as Aphek, as far as the territories of the Amorites;
and all the land of Gilead belonging to the Philistines, and all Lebanon toward the sunrise, from Gilgal beneath Mount Hermon to the entrance of Hamath.
All who live in the mountains, from Lebanon as far as Misrephoth-maim [?], all the Sidonians—I will destroy them before the Israelites, as I told you.
Now divide this land among them and give it as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
From the Jordan to the Great Sea toward the sunset, he will give it to them, and it will belong to them. The Great Sea will be their boundary.
To those two tribes, Reuben and Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, Moses gave land beyond the Jordan.
On the side toward the sunrise, Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave them land from Aroer, which is across the river Arnon, and the city in the middle of the valley, and all the plain from Medeba;
all the cities of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the territory of the Ammonites;
and Gilead, the territory of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, all the mountains of Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah;

the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Edrei and Ashtaroth. He was left from the race of the giants, and Moses killed and destroyed him. But the Israelites did not destroy the Geshurites, the Maacathites, or the Canaanites among them. The king of Geshur and Maacah lives among the Israelites to this very day.

Only the tribe of Levi received no allotted inheritance, because the Lord, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as the Lord told them. Thus they received their portions, as Moses allotted them to the Israelites on the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
Moses gave land to the tribe of Reuben according to their clans.
Their territory extended from Aroer, which faces the Arnon Valley, and its city within the Arnon Valley, and included all the plain as far as Heshbon;
all the cities in the plain, Dibon, Bamon, Baal, and the houses of Meelmot;
Bashan, Kedemoth, and Mephaath;
And Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Seradoth, and Zion on Mount Enab.
Beth-peor, Ashdoth, Pisgah, and Beth-jeshimoth;

all the cities of the plain and the whole kingdom of Sihon, king of the Amorites, whom Moses killed, along with the rulers of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, rulers of the coastal region, who lived in Sihon.
They also killed Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, with the sword.
The territory of Reuben was the Jordan and its border. This was the inheritance of the descendants of Reuben according to their clans, together with their cities.
Moses gave land to the descendants of Gad according to their clans.
Their territory included Jazer, all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites as far as Arabah, which faces Arad;
and from Heshbon to Araboth, which faces Mizpah, and Betonim, and from Maan to the territory of Dibon.

And in Adom, Otrga, and Abayin [?], and Succoth and Zaphon, and the rest of the kingdom of Sihon, king of Heshbon; and the Jordan and their border as far as one end of the Sea of Chinnereth, across the Jordan on the east.

This was the inheritance of the descendants of Gad according to their clans. They turned their backs before their enemies, for their cities and the hill country of their cities belonged to them according to their clans.
Moses gave land to the half-tribe of Manasseh according to their clans.
Their territory extended from Mahanaim and included the whole kingdom of Bashan, the whole kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair in Bashan—sixty towns.

And half the land of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the towns of Og’s kingdom in Bashan, belonged to the descendants of Machir, the son of Manasseh—to half the descendants of Machir, the son of Manasseh, according to their clans.
These are the ones to whom Moses gave an inheritance beyond the Jordan, in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan east of Jericho.
These are the inheritances allotted to the Israelites in the land of Canaan by Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral households of the tribes of Israel.
They received their inheritances according to their allotted portions, as the Lord commanded through Joshua, for the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh beyond the Jordan.
But they gave the Levites no allotted portion.
For Joseph's descendants formed two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. They gave the Levites no allotted portion of land except the towns set apart for them to live in.
The Israelites did as the Lord commanded Moses, and they divided the land.

The people of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, “You yourself know what the Lord said to Moses, the man of God, concerning me and you at Kadesh-barnea.

I was forty years old when Moses, the Lord's servant, sent me from Kadesh-barnea to inspect that land. My brothers who went up with me reported to him according to their own thoughts and turned the people's hearts away, but I committed myself to following the Lord my God.
Moses swore that day, saying, ‘The land into which you went up will be your allotted inheritance and your children's forever, because I committed myself to following the Lord our God.’
Now the Lord has kept me alive these forty-five years since the Lord spoke this word to Moses, while Israel traveled in the wilderness.
And now, today, I am eighty-five years old.
I am still as strong as when Moses sent me. I am just as strong now for going out to battle and for coming back.

Now I ask you for this hill country, as the Lord said on that day, for you yourself heard this word at that time. The Anakim are there now, and their cities are large and fortified. If the Lord is with me, I will destroy them, as the Lord told me.”
Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and gave him Hebron as his allotted inheritance, until today, until this very day, because he followed the command of the Lord, the God of Israel.
Hebron's former name was the city of Argob, and it was the mountain of cities for those among the Anakim. And the land rested from warfare.
The territory of the tribe of Judah, according to their clans, extended from the borders of the Edomites, from the wilderness of Zin to Kadesh toward the south.
Their southwestern border extended to one end of the Salt Sea, from the road that leads southwest.
It passes in front of Akrabbim, goes out to Senak, ascends from the southwest to Kadesh-barnea, goes out to Hezron, ascends to Sarada, and goes out to Arab-kadesh.
It goes toward Azmon and comes out at the valley of Egypt. Their boundary ends at the sea. This is their southern boundary.
Their eastern border was the whole Salt Sea as far as the Jordan. Their northern border ran from the road toward the sea and from one end of the Jordan.
Their border ascends to Beth-hoglah, passes toward the north, and ascends to the stone of Bohan son of Reuben.

Their boundary goes up along the fourth part of the Valley of Achor and descends to Gilgal, opposite the ascent of Adummim, which is south of the valley. It goes out to the spring of Helios and ends at En-rogel.

Their boundary goes up through the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, south of Jebus, which is Jerusalem. Their boundary comes out at the summit of the mountain facing the Valley of Hinnom on the west, at the northern end of the land of the Rephaim.
Their boundary runs from that mountain summit to the spring of Nephtoah and reaches Mount Ephron. Their boundary runs to Baal, which is Kiriath-jearim.
Their boundary passes westward from Baal and passes along the boundary of Asaretus, south of the town of Jearim and north of Chesalon. It descends toward the town of Eliu and passes toward Libah.

Their boundary goes out south of Ekron and turns north. Their boundary goes out to Succoth, passes southward, and goes out to Libnah. Their boundary ends at the sea. Their boundary on the seaward side is the Great Sea, which forms their border.
This is the boundary surrounding the descendants of Judah, according to their clans.
To Caleb son of Jephunneh he gave a share among the descendants of Judah, according to the Lord's command. Joshua gave him the city of Arba, the chief city of Anak, which is Hebron.
Caleb son of Jephunneh drove out from there the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, Talmai, and Ahiman.
From there Caleb went up against those who lived in Debir. Debir's former name was Kiriath-sepher.
Caleb said, “Whoever takes Kiriath-sepher, defeats it, and brings it under control, I will give him my daughter Achsah as his wife.”
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, took it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as his wife.
Afterward, when she was about to leave, she consulted him, saying, “I will ask my father for fields.” She cried out while on the donkey, and Caleb said to her, “What is the matter with you?”

She said to him, “Give me a blessing. Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me Bothanis.” He gave her Upper Gonethlan and Lower Gonethlan from the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Judah.
Their cities—the cities of the tribe of the descendants of Judah within the borders of Edom, in the wilderness—were Beseleel, Ara, and Hazor;
and Icam, Regma, and Aruel;
and Kadesh, Asrionem, and Minan;
and Balmanan, with their villages;
And the towns of Hezron, that is, Hazor.
and Sen, Shema, and Moladah;
and Seri and Bephalad;
and Colasoeda and Beersheba, with their villages;
Balah and Bacob, with their hills, and Azem;
and Elebohidad, Bethel, and Hormah;
and Ziklag, Macerm, and Sitenah;
and Labos, Sale, and Hermoth: twenty-nine cities, with their villages.
In the plain: Eshtaol, Zorah, and Asa;
and Upper Rimmon, Idutot, and Mahans;
And Jarmuth, Adullam, Mamre, Socoh, and Azekah.
and Sacarm and Gederah, with its hills: fourteen cities, with their villages.
Zenan, Hadashah, and Migdal-gad;
And Adalel, Mizpah, Joktheel, and Makesa.
And Bozkath, Jedeha, and Doleah.
And Cabra, Machas, and Machos.
And Gedor, Bogadiel, Naamah, and Makkedah: sixteen towns and their villages.
Libnah, Ethek, and Anoch.
And Adnah and Nezib.
And Ilem, Aqezem, Bethesar, and Elom—ten cities and their villages.
Ekron and its villages and their hamlets.
From Ekron, Jamnia and everything near Ashdod, and their villages.
Ashdod and its villages and its hamlets, and Gaza and its villages and its hamlets, as far as the river of Egypt; the Great Sea forms its boundary.
And in the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, and Socoh.
And Renah and the City of the Book, which is Debir.
And Anon, Sheqemah, and Esamah.
And Goshen, Holon, and Giloh—eleven cities and their villages.
Erem, Rhemna, and Soma.
And Janim, Beth-tappuah, and Aphekah.
And Humtah, Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, and Zior: nine towns and their hills.
Mehor, Carmel, Ozib, and Juttah.
And Jezreel, Jokdeam, and Zanoah.
And Gibeah and Timnah—nine cities and their villages.
And Halhul, Beth-zur, and Gedor.
And Magedoth, Beth-anoth, and Eltekon—six cities and their villages.

Tekoa and Ephrathah, which is Bethlehem, and Peor, Etam, Kulon, Taton, Sobehe, Karem, Gallim, Ether, and Manocho—eleven cities and their villages. Kiriath-baal, which is Kiriath-jearim, and Sobethah—two cities and their hamlets.
And Baldagis, Therabeam, and Emon.
And Seciozan, Nephlazan, and their cities, Salem and Kadesh—seven cities and their villages.
The descendants of Judah were unable to destroy the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem, and the Jebusites remained in Jerusalem to this day.
The boundary of the descendants of Joseph ran from the Jordan toward Jericho, on its eastern side, and went up from Jericho into the mountains in the wilderness, to Bethel, Luz.
It went out to Bethel and passed along the boundary of Cheronti.
Seven rivers pass across their boundary, within the territory of Lower Beth-horon, and their outlets are at the sea.
The descendants of Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh, received their inheritance.
This was the boundary of Ephraim according to their clans. The boundary of their inheritance ran from east of Ataroth, through Eroch, Upper Beth-horon, and Gezer.
Their boundary passes toward the sea from north of Terma, then passes eastward to Taanath and into Elas, and continues eastward into Janoah.
It continues into Macho and Ataroth and their surrounding settlements, reaches Jericho, and ends at the Jordan.
From Tappuah their boundary goes westward along Kanah and ends at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim according to their clans.
And the towns set apart for the descendants of Ephraim within the inheritance of the descendants of Manasseh—all their towns and their villages.

Ephraim did not destroy the Canaanites who lived in Gezer. The Canaanites lived among Ephraim to this day, until Pharaoh king of Egypt came up, captured the city, and burned it with fire. They killed the Canaanites, the Perizzites, and those living in Gezer, and Pharaoh gave the city to his daughter as her dowry.
This was the territory of the tribe of the descendants of Manasseh, for he was Joseph’s firstborn.
For Machir, Manasseh’s firstborn, the father of Gilead, because he was a warrior in Gilead and Bashan.

And an allotment fell to the remaining descendants of Manasseh according to their clans: to the descendants of Abiezer, the descendants of Helek, the descendants of Asriel, the descendants of Shechem, and the descendants of Hepher.
These were their males according to their clans.
Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, only daughters. These were the names of Zelophehad’s daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

They stood before Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the leaders, and said, “The Lord commanded through Moses that an inheritance be given to us among our brothers.” So, according to the Lord’s command, they gave them an inheritance among their father’s brothers.
The allotment fell from Hanas [?], and the field of Lebek [?] from Gilead, which is beyond the Jordan.
For the daughters of the descendants of Manasseh inherited property among their brothers. The land of Gilead belonged to the remaining descendants of Manasseh.
The boundary of the descendants of Manasseh was Delanath, opposite the descendants of Hanath. It runs along the boundary of Jamin and into Jashib, to the spring of Tappuah.
It belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah, on Manasseh’s boundary, belonged to the descendants of Ephraim.

Their boundary descends to the valley of Kanah on the south, and to the valley of Jariel and Tereminthon belonging to Ephraim, among the towns of Manasseh. Manasseh’s boundary runs northward beside the river and ends at the sea. The southern side belongs to Ephraim, and the northern side to Manasseh, with the sea as their boundary. [They meet Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.] Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh has Tohan and its surrounding settlements, the inhabitants of Dor and its surrounding settlements, the inhabitants of Gedo and its surrounding settlements, and a third part of Mepheta and its surrounding settlements.
The descendants of Manasseh could not destroy these cities, and the Canaanites came and lived in that land.
Israel overpowered them and subjected them to forced labor, but did not utterly destroy them.
The descendants of Joseph addressed Joshua and said to him, “Why have you given us only one inheritance and one measured portion, when I am a numerous people and the Lord has blessed me?”
He said to them, “Go up into the forest and clear it for yourselves, if the hill country of Ephraim is too cramped for you.”
They said, “The hill country of Ephraim is not enough for us, and the Canaanites who live in it have choice horses and iron at Beth-shean and in its surrounding villages, in the valley of Jezreel.”
Joshua said to the descendants of Joseph, “If you are a numerous people and have great strength, you shall not have only one inheritance.”
“For the field is yours. It is a forest, and you will clear it for yourself. It will be yours until you destroy the Canaanites, for they have choice horses, but you yourself are stronger than they.”
The whole assembly of the Israelites gathered at Shiloh and set up the Tent of Testimony there. They had subdued the land.
Seven tribes of the Israelites remained who had not received their inheritance.
Joshua said to the Israelites, “How long will you delay taking possession of the land that the Lord our God has given you?”
“Choose three men from each tribe from among yourselves. Let them set out and travel through the land, and write a description of it before me according to their survey.”
They inspected it and came to him, and he divided it into seven portions for them. Judah established its territory to the south, and the descendants of Joseph established theirs to the north.
“But you must divide the land into seven portions and bring it here to me, and I will assign you an inheritance before the Lord your God.”

For the descendants of Levi have no share among you, because service as priests of the Lord is their share. Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance across the Jordan to the east, which Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave them.

The men set out and went, and Joshua instructed those going to survey the land. He told them, “Go, survey the land, and return to me here, so that I may cast lots for your portions before the Lord at Shiloh.”
They went and surveyed the land and inspected it. They wrote a description of it in a book, town by town, and brought it to Joshua.
Joshua cast lots for their portions before the Lord at Shiloh.
The first lot fell to Benjamin, according to his clans. The territory allotted to them lay between Judah and Joseph.

Their northern boundary began at the Jordan. Their boundary went up along the southern side of Jericho, continued northward, and ascended the mountain toward the west. It ended at Madbaritis of Bethon.
From there it passed over the hills of Luz, toward the southern ridge of Luz, which is Bethel. It descended to the boundary of Ataroth of Horech, which is in the hills south of Lower Beth-horon.

Their boundary passed along the side facing west, south of the mountain opposite Beth-horon on the south. It ended at Kiriath-baal, which is Kiriath-jearim, a town belonging to the descendants of Judah. This was their western boundary.
Their southern boundary began at Kiriath-baal. Their boundary passed over Gain to the spring of Nephtoah.

Their boundary descended along the side opposite Napesannem, north of the side of Emek-rephaim. It descended from Napin along the southern ridge of the Jebusites and went down to the spring of En-rogel.
It passes to the spring of Beth-shemesh and goes to Geliloth, which is opposite the ascent of Adummim, and descends to the stone of Bohan, of the descendants of Reuben.
It passes along the western side of Beth-arabah, and their boundary descends along the western side of the sea.
Their boundary ended at the road to the Sea of Alon on the north and at the southern bank of the Jordan. This was the southern boundary.
The Jordan was their boundary on the eastern side. This was the boundary surrounding the inheritance of the descendants of Benjamin, according to their clans.
The towns belonging to the descendants of Benjamin, according to their clans, were Jericho, Beth-geo, and Amekasis;
Beth-barah, Sarah, and Besana;
Ain, Parah, and Ephrathah;
Karaphah, Chephirah, Moni, and Geba: twelve towns with their villages.
Gibeon and Ramah;
Mesema, Beeroth, and Moqe;
Bera, Qaphen, Qana, Seleqan, and Terelah;
Jebus, which is the city of Jerusalem, Gibeath, and the town of Jearim: thirteen towns with their villages. This was the inheritance of the descendants of Benjamin, according to their clans.
The second lot fell to the descendants of Simeon, and their inheritance was within the territory of the descendants of Judah.
Their allotted portion included Beersheba, Shema, and Coladam;
Arsolah, Balah, and Iason;
Lula, Bul, and Hormah;
Ziklag, Beth-marcaboth, and Hazar-susim.
And Betharoth and their fields: thirteen towns and their villages.
And Rimmon, Talca, Ether, and Ashan: four towns and their villages.
And the territory surrounding these towns extended as far as Balek and passed beyond Bameth toward the south. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Simeon.
For the allotment of the descendants of Judah was larger than theirs, and the descendants of Simeon received their inheritance within their allotment.
The third allotment fell to Zebulun, according to their clans. The boundary of their inheritance was Esedek; Gola was their boundary.
From the sea and Maralah, it joins Beth-arabah, which is in the valley opposite Jokneam.
It turns from Sarid toward the eastern side of Beth-shemesh, to the boundary of Chesulloth, passes through Daberath, and goes up to Japhia.
From there it passes along the eastern side of the city of Geber, which is toward the north, and passes to Rimmon of Amteryoza.
Their boundary passes to the west of Amoth, and its endpoint is at Jiphthah-el toward the south.
And Nahalal, Shimron, Jericho, and Bethlehem.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Zebulun according to their clans: the cities and their surrounding villages.
The fourth allotment fell to Issachar.
Their territory included Jezreel, Chesulloth, and Shunem.
And Agin, Sionan, and Rehete.
And Anaharath, Daberath, Kishion, and Ebez.
And Rimmon, Emarek, and Beersheba.
Their boundary reached Tabor and Salim, which lies toward the west, and Beth-shemesh. Their boundary ended at the Jordan.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Issachar, according to their clans, together with their towns and their villages.
The fifth allotment fell to Asher.
Their boundary began at Helkath, Hali, Beten, and Achshaph.
And Allammelech, Amihal, and Mishal. It reached Carmel on the west, and Shihor-libnath.
On the east it turned toward Beth-dagon and reached Zebulun, Emgege, and Iphtah-el toward the north. Their boundary entered the plain of Beth-emek and Neiel and passed into Kobem and Asomel.
And Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Great Sidon.
Their boundary turns into Ramah and extends to the spring of Misphat and the Tyrians. Their boundary turns into Iasiph, and the boundary ends at the sea, and from Leb and Achzib.
And Archob, Aphek, and Raau.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Asher, according to their clans, together with their towns and their villages.
The sixth allotment fell to Naphtali.
Their boundary was Mohalam, Mola, Besemiin, Arme, Nabo, and Iaphtheme, as far as Aodem, and its endpoint was the Jordan.
Their boundary turned westward toward Aznoth-tabor and passed from there beyond Iknaka. It reached Zebulun on the south; Asher bordered them on the west, and the Jordan on the east.
And the cities of Tyre that had walls: Tyre, Hammath-rakkath, and Chinnereth.
And Armath, Arahel, and Hazor.
And Kedesh, Edrei, and En-hazor.
And Iron, Migdal-horem, Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Naphtali.
The seventh lot fell to Dan.
Their territory included Zorah, Eshtaol, and Ir-shemesh.
And Shaalabbin, Ammon, and Silathah.
And Elon, Timnathah, and Ekron.
And Eltekeh, Gibbethon, and Gibbelan.
And Azor, Bene-berak, and Gath-rimmon.
And from the sea, Jarkon, with the boundary near Joppa.

This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Dan, according to their clans, with their towns and villages. The descendants of Dan did not overcome the Amorites, who pressed them into the hill country. The Amorites did not allow them to come down into the lowlands, and took from them one section within the boundaries of their allotment.

The descendants of Dan went and killed the people of Lachish. They took their town, struck it with the edge of the sword, settled in it, and named it Leshem-dan. The Amorites insisted on remaining in Aijalon and Shaalbim, but Ephraim's hand grew strong against them, and they became subject to tribute.
They went to divide the land within its boundaries, and the Israelites gave Joshua his allotment among them, at the LORD's command.
They gave him the town he requested, Timnath-serah, in the hill country of Ephraim. He built up that town and lived in it.

These are their portions, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the ancestral families of the tribes of Israel gave them as an inheritance, according to their allotments, at Shiloh before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of witness. And they went to divide the land.
The LORD spoke to Joshua and said to him:
“Tell the Israelites: ‘Set aside the cities of refuge that I told you about through Moses.
They are a refuge for a killer who has killed a person unknowingly, without intending to. Establish cities of refuge for yourselves.

He shall flee to one of these cities, stand at the entrance of the city gate, and tell his case to the elders of that city. The people shall take him in among them and give him a place, and he shall live with them.
When the avenger of blood pursues him, do not hand him over, because he killed his fellow unknowingly and had not hated him before.

He shall remain in that town until he appears before the assembly for judgment, and until the death of the high priest serving in those days. Then the killer shall return to his town and his house, to the town from which he fled. The avenger of blood shall not kill the killer before he stands before the assembly for judgment.’”
They set apart Kedesh in Galilee, in the hill country of Naphtali; Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim; and Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.

Across the Jordan from Jericho, to the east, he assigned Bezer in the wilderness plain, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.

These were the places the Israelites chose, also for the foreigner living among them, so that any killer who had unknowingly killed a person could flee there, and the avenger of blood would not kill him before he stood before the assembly for judgment.
The representatives of the descendants of Levi came to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the representatives of the tribes and ancestral households of the people of Israel.
They spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, “The Lord commanded through Moses that we should be given cities in which to live, and their pasturelands for our livestock.”
At the LORD's command, the Israelites gave the Levites these towns and their surrounding pasturelands.

The allotment fell to the clans of the descendants of Kohath. The priests, the descendants of Aaron, and the Levites received thirteen towns as their allotment from the tribe of Judah, the tribe of Simeon, and the tribe of Benjamin.
The remaining descendants of Kohath received thirteen towns as their allotment from the tribe of Ephraim, the tribe of Dan, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
The descendants of Gershon received as their allotment thirteen towns from the tribe of Issachar, from the tribe of Asher, from the tribe of Naphtali, and from the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
The descendants of Merari, according to their clans, received as their allotment twelve towns from the tribe of Reuben, from the tribe of Gad, and from the tribe of Zebulun.
The Israelites gave the Levites towns and their pasturelands as their allotment, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The tribe of the descendants of Judah, the tribe of the descendants of Simeon, and some from the tribe of the descendants of Benjamin gave these cities, which were named:
For the descendants of Aaron, from the clan of Kohath among the descendants of Levi, since the allotment fell to them.
They gave them the land of Kiriath-arba, the hill of the towns of Anak, which is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, together with its surrounding pasturelands.
But Joshua gave the fields of the town and its cultivated lands to the descendants of Caleb son of Jephunneh as their territory.
To the descendants of Aaron he gave Hebron, a city of refuge for a killer, with its allotted lands, and Libnah with its allotted lands.
And Elom with its allotted lands, and Tema with its allotted lands.
And Holon with its allotted lands, and Debir with its allotted lands.
And Asa with its allotted lands, and Tani with its allotted lands, and Beth-shemesh with its allotted lands: nine towns from the two clans and from these tribes.
And from the tribe of Benjamin, Gibeon with its allotted lands, and Geba with its allotted lands.
And Anathoth with its allotted lands, and Almon with its allotted lands: four towns.
All the towns belonging to the descendants of Aaron, the priests, numbered thirteen.
For the clan of the descendants of Kohath, the Levites who remained of the descendants of Kohath, the towns for their priests came from the tribe of Ephraim.
He gave them Shechem, a city of refuge for a killer, with its allotted lands, and Gezer with its allotted lands.
And Kibzaim with its allotted lands, and Beth-horon with its allotted lands: four towns.
And from the tribe of Dan, Elkothem with its allotted lands, and Gibbethon with its allotted lands, and Aijalon with its allotted lands, and Gath-rimmon with its allotted lands: four towns.
And from the half-tribe of Manasseh, Taanach with its allotted lands, and Jebotha with its allotted lands: two towns.
There were ten towns in all, with their allotted lands, assigned to the remaining clans of the descendants of Kohath.
For the descendants of Gershon, the Levites, from the half-tribe of Manasseh: the towns set apart for a killer, Golan in Bashan with its allotted lands, and Bosor with its allotted lands: two towns.
And from the clan of Issachar: Kishion and the land set apart with it, and Daberath and the land set apart with it.
And Jarmuth with its allotted lands, and En-gannim with its allotted lands: four towns. And from the tribe of Asher, Besela with its allotted lands, and Abdon with its allotted lands.
And Helkath with its allotted lands, and Rehob with its allotted lands: four towns.
And from the tribe of Naphtali, the town set apart for a killer, Kedesh in Galilee with its allotted lands, and Phemath with its allotted lands, and Aemon with its allotted lands: three towns.
All the towns belonging to Gershon, according to their clans, numbered thirteen towns.
For the clans of Merari, the remaining Levites, from the tribe of Zebulun: Maan with its pasturelands, and Kedesh with its pasturelands.
And Sela with its pasturelands.

And beyond the Jordan, opposite Jericho, from the tribe of Reuben: Bezer, a city of refuge for a manslayer, in the wilderness of Mison, with its pasturelands; Jazer with its pasturelands; Gadeon with its pasturelands; and Ausapha with its pasturelands—four cities.

And from the tribe of Gad: Ramoth in Gilead, a city of refuge for a manslayer, with its pasturelands; Kamin with its pasturelands; Heshbon with its pasturelands; and Jazer with its pasturelands—four cities in all.
All the cities belonging to the descendants of Merari, according to their clans—the remaining members of the tribe of Levi—were twelve cities as their allotted territory.
All the cities of the Levites within the territory of the Israelites were forty-eight cities, together with the pasturelands surrounding those cities.
Each city had pasturelands surrounding it; this was so for all these cities. And Joshua finished dividing the land according to their territories.
The Israelites gave Joshua his allotted portion at the LORD’s command. They gave him the city he requested, Timnath-serah, in the hill country of Ephraim. Joshua built that city and lived in it.

Joshua took those flint knives with which they had circumcised the Israelites who were with him on the journey in the wilderness, for they had not been circumcised in the wilderness, and he placed them in Timnath-serah.
The LORD gave the Israelites all the land that he had sworn to give their ancestors. They took possession of it and lived in it.
The LORD gave them rest on every side, just as he had sworn to their ancestors. Not one of all their enemies stood against them, for the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hands.
