Not one word of all the good things that the LORD had spoken to the Israelites remained unfulfilled; all of it came to them.
Then Joshua summoned the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
He said to them, “You have obeyed everything that Moses, the LORD’s servant, commanded you, and you have obeyed my voice in everything that I commanded you.
You have not abandoned your brothers throughout these many days, right up to this very day, and you have kept the commandment of the LORD your God.
Now the LORD your God has given your brothers rest, as he told them. So now return and go to your homes and to your territory, the land that Moses, the LORD’s servant, gave you beyond the Jordan.

But take great care to carry out the commandment and the law that Moses, the LORD’s servant, commanded you to follow: to love the LORD our God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to follow him, and to serve him with all your heart and all your soul.”
Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their homes.

Moses had given land in Bashan to half the tribe of Manasseh, while Joshua had given land to the other half with their brothers beyond the Jordan, toward the sea. When Joshua sent them away to their homes, he blessed them and spoke to them.
They went to their homes with great wealth, very many livestock, gold, silver, bronze, iron, and a great quantity of clothing. They shared the plunder of their enemies with their brothers.

The descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh returned, leaving the Israelites at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, to go to the land of Gilead, to their own territory and their inheritance, which they had received at the LORD’s command through Moses.

They reached Gilead by the Jordan, in the land of Canaan. There the descendants of Gad, the descendants of Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar beside the Jordan—a large, conspicuous altar.

The Israelites heard that the descendants of Gad, the descendants of Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had built an altar within the territory of Canaan, near Gilead by the Jordan, across from the Israelites.
When the Israelites heard this, all the Israelites gathered at Shiloh to go up and fight against them.
The Israelites sent Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, to the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead.
Ten representatives went with him, one representative from the ancestral households of each tribe of Israel. These men were representatives of their ancestral households and leaders of Israel.
They came to the descendants of Gad, the descendants of Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, and spoke to them, saying:

“This is what the whole assembly of the Lord says: What is this offense that you have committed before the God of Israel, abandoning the Lord today and building yourselves an altar, so that you deny the Lord today?”
Do you consider the sin at Peor a small thing? We have not been cleansed of it to this day, and a plague came upon the congregation of the Lord.
And now you have abandoned following the Lord. Because you have rebelled against the Lord today, tomorrow a plague will come upon all Israel.

Now, if your territory is too small for you, cross over into the land belonging to the Lord, where the Lord's tabernacle stands, and receive an inheritance among us. Do not rebel against the Lord or abandon the Lord by building an altar apart from the altar of the Lord our God.
Did not Achan son of Zerah sin and do wrong by taking some of what was forbidden? Wrath came upon the whole congregation of Israel, although he alone had sinned. Did he alone die because of his sin?
The descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the representatives of Israel, saying:

The Lord is God and Lord, and he is the God of gods. The Lord knows, and Israel too will know, that what we have done before the Lord was not an act of rebellion or wrongdoing. If it was otherwise, may he not save us today.

If we have built an altar for ourselves to rebel against the Lord our God, or to offer sacrificial offerings on it, or to offer sacrifices of well-being upon it, may the Lord himself call us to account.
“It was only out of fear of the Lord that we did this, saying, ‘Lest in the future your children say to our children: What have you to do with the Lord, the God of Israel?’”

For the Lord established a boundary between you and us—the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh—the Jordan, and you have no share in the Lord. Your children will make our children strangers to the worship of the Lord (so that they do not drive them out).
“And we said, ‘Let us do this and build this altar, not for an offering and not for a sacrifice.’”

Rather, let this be a witness between us and you, and among our children after us, so that they may worship the Lord before him with your offerings and your sacrifices of well-being, and so that your children will not say to our children in the future, 'You have no share in the Lord.'

And we said, “If it happens in the future that they speak to us or to our children, they are to say to them, ‘Look at the likeness of the Lord’s altar that our ancestors made, not for offerings and not for sacrifices, but to be a witness between us and you.’”

Far be it from us to abandon following the Lord today, to rebel against the Lord, or to build ourselves an altar for offerings, sacrifices of peace, or sacrifices of well-being, apart from the altar of the Lord our God that stands before his tabernacle.

When Phinehas the priest and all the representatives of the assembly and the leaders of Israel who were with him heard the words spoken to them by the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, they were quiet.

Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest, said to the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, 'Today we know that the Lord is with us, because you have not committed this sin before the Lord, and because you have delivered Israel from the Lord's hand.'
Phinehas son of Eleazar and the representatives returned from the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, from Gilead to the Israelites in the land of Canaan, and reported to them.

This report reassured the Israelites. When they told the Israelites, they blessed the God of the Israelites and said, “Then we will not go up against them to fight them and destroy the land of the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.” And they continued to live in it.
Joshua named that altar belonging to Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and they said, “It is a witness among them that the Lord is their God.”
After this, many days after the Lord, the God of Israel, had given them rest from all their enemies around them, Joshua grew old and was advanced in years.
He called all the Israelites, their elders, their representatives, their scribes, and their rulers, and said to them, “Look, I have grown old, and my days have passed.
You yourselves have seen everything the Lord our God has done to the nations before us, for the Lord our God fought against them for us.

Look, they have left for you the nations that remain within your territories, for each of your tribes, along with all the nations I uprooted, from the Jordan [?] the Great Sea, your boundary toward the setting sun.

The Lord your God himself will destroy them before you until they are wiped out. He will send wild animals against them until he destroys them and their kings before you, and you will take possession of their land, as the Lord our God told us.
Be very steadfast in observing and doing everything written in the book of the law of Moses, so that you do not turn away from it, either to the left or to the right.
Do not associate with these nations that remain among you. Do not let the names of their gods be mentioned among you, and do not swear by them, bow down to them, or worship them.
Instead, follow the Lord your God, as you have done to this day.
The Lord himself will destroy great and powerful nations before you. As for you, no one has been able to stand against you to this day.
One man among you will put a thousand to flight, because the Lord our God fights for us, as he told us.
Take great care to love the Lord our God.
But if you turn back and abandon him, associating with these nations that remain among you, intermarrying with them and joining yourselves to them,

then know for yourselves that the Lord will no longer destroy these nations before you. They will become a snare and a trap for you, nails in your heels, and they will pierce your eyes, until you perish from the blessed land that the Lord your God has given you.

I am going the way of everyone on earth. Know with all your heart and all your soul that not one word has failed of all the good things the Lord our God told you. Everything has come to us, and there is nothing of it that we have not received.

Just as every good word that the Lord your God spoke to you has come true for you, so the Lord your God will bring upon you every threatened disaster, until he destroys you from this blessed land that the Lord has given you.

If you abandon the covenant of your God that he commanded you to keep, and if you go and worship other gods and bow down to them, the Lord will rage against you in anger and will quickly destroy you from the land he has given you.”
Joshua gathered all the people of Israel at Shiloh. He called the elders of Israel, their representatives, and their scribes, and had them stand before the Lord.

Joshua said to all the people, “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: ‘Long ago your ancestors lived beyond the river—Terah, the father of Abraham and the father of Nahor—and they worshiped other gods.
I took your father Abraham from beyond the river and led him throughout the land of Canaan, and I multiplied his descendants.

And I gave him Isaac, and to Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau Mount Seir as his inheritance. But Jacob and his children went down into Egypt. There they became a great people, grew numerous and strong, and the Egyptians oppressed them.
And I killed the Egyptians because of what they had done to them.
After this I brought you out, and he brought out your ancestors. You entered the sea, and the Egyptians pursued you. You followed behind your ancestors with horses and chariots into the Red Sea.

We cried out to the Lord, and he sent a cloud and darkness between us and the Egyptians. He brought the sea over them and covered them. Your own eyes saw everything the Lord did in the land of Egypt, and you lived in the wilderness for many days.

He brought you into the land of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan. Moses fought against them, and the Lord delivered them into our hands. You took possession of their land and destroyed them before you.
Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, rose up and fought against Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor and summoned him to curse us.
But the Lord your God did not wish to destroy you. He blessed us abundantly, rescued us from their hands, and delivered them over to us.

You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The inhabitants of Jericho fought against us, along with the Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites, Hittites, and Girgashites. But the Lord delivered them into our hands.
He sent hornets against them ahead of us and drove out the twelve kings of the Amorites before us—not by your sword or by your bow.
He gave you a land for which you had not labored and cities you had not built, and you lived in them. You eat from vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant.
Now fear the Lord and worship him in righteousness and uprightness. Put away the foreign gods your ancestors worshiped beyond the River and in Egypt, and worship the Lord.

But if you are unwilling to worship the Lord, choose for yourselves today whom you will worship: whether the gods of your ancestors beyond the River or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you live. But I and my household will worship the Lord, for he is holy.
The people answered and said, “Far be it from us to abandon the Lord and worship other gods!”

But for us, the Lord is our God, for he is God. He brought us and our ancestors out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, and performed all the great signs for us. He protected us along the whole road we traveled and among all the nations through which we passed.
The Lord drove out before us the Amorites and all the nations that lived in the land. We too will therefore worship the Lord, for he is our God.
Joshua said to the people, “You cannot worship the Lord, for he is holy. Because you have provoked him to jealousy, he will not forgive your sins and your offenses.”
“If you abandon the Lord and worship other gods, he will go and afflict you and destroy you in place of the good he has done for you.”
The people said to Joshua, “Nevertheless, we will worship the Lord.”
Joshua said to the people, “You yourselves are witnesses against yourselves that you yourselves have chosen the Lord, to worship him.” And they said, “We are witnesses.”
He said to them, “Now put away the foreign gods that are among you, and direct your hearts toward the Lord, the God of Israel.”
The people said to Joshua, “We will worship the Lord our God and obey his voice.”
Joshua made a covenant with the people that day and gave them laws and ordinances at Shiloh, before the tabernacle of the God of Israel.
Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of the Lord. Then Joshua took a large stone and set it up beneath the terebinth tree before the Lord.

Joshua said to all the people, “Look, this stone is a witness against you, for it has heard everything said by the Lord as he spoke to you today. It will be a witness against you in days to come if you are false to the Lord my God.”
Joshua sent the people away, and they all went to their own settlements.
Israel worshiped the Lord throughout Joshua’s lifetime and throughout the lifetimes of the elders who outlived Joshua, and all those who had seen all the work the Lord had done for Israel.
After this, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died at the age of one hundred and ten.

They buried him within the boundaries of his inheritance, in Timnath-serah, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gilead. There, in the tomb where they buried him, they placed with him the stone knives with which he had circumcised the Israelites at Gilgal when they came out of Egypt, as the Lord had commanded him. They remain there to this day.

They also buried Joseph’s bones, which they had brought out of Egypt, in Shechem, in a parcel of farmland that Jacob had bought from the Amorites living in Shechem for one hundred sheep. He had given it to Joseph as his portion.

After this, when Eleazar son of Aaron, the high priest, died, they buried him in the land of Gabaor, which he had given to his son Phinehas in the hill country of Ephraim. At that time the Israelites took the ark of the Lord and carried it with them. Phinehas became high priest in place of Eleazar his father until he died, and they buried him in Gabaor, in their land. All the Israelites went to their homes and their towns. The Israelites worshiped Astarte and Ashtaroth and the gods of the nations around them. The Lord handed them over to Eglon king of Moab, and he enslaved them for eighteen years.
